title: Access control model — RBAC evaluated, two roles adopted
question: Does jobby need role-based access control?
decision: No RBAC matrix. Keep three concerns separate: tenant isolation (security), entitlement (commercial), and a two-value role claim (user | admin). One can(ctx, action) function is the single call site.
why_not_rbac: RBAC solves many users sharing resources with different rights; jobby has one user per tenant and no shared resources
The security boundary is already absolute — tenantRoot() from the session (BL-020) — and a role matrix on top of it protects nothing new
Capability differences here are commercial (plan, key attached), not organisational; modelling them as permissions confuses billing with security

roles.user: owns exactly one tenant; every capability difference comes from entitlement, not role
roles.admin: platform staff — usage counters, feature flags, queue health, error rates

hard_rule.statement: admin must NEVER imply the ability to read tenant files
hard_rule.why: an admin bypass silently undoes the BL-020 isolation boundary
hard_rule.if_support_needs_access: explicit, time-boxed, audited impersonation grant that the tenant can see — not a permission bit

revisit_when.trigger: a recruiter or agency manages several searchers
revisit_when.note: that is many-to-many user<->tenant membership — relationship-shaped (ReBAC), not role-shaped; it changes the tenancy model rather than adding roles

alternatives_rejected.why: no user for it; ceremony over an already-absolute boundary

alternatives_rejected.option: roles as the gate for paid features
alternatives_rejected.why: conflates billing state with security state; plan changes would become permission migrations
defeats tenant isolation, the one guarantee the product makes
